title: 2 Chronicles Bible Quiz - Chapter 19
description: Ten questions on 2 Chronicles 19: Jehu's rebuke of Jehoshaphat and the judges Jehoshaphat set over the land.

questions.text: Where did Jehoshaphat return in peace at the start of the chapter?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 19:1 says Jehoshaphat the king of Judah returned to his house in peace to Jerusalem.

answers.text: To Ahab's palace in Samaria
To his house in Jerusalem
To the camp at Ramoth Gilead
To his fortress in Hebron

questions.text: Who went out to meet Jehoshaphat when he returned?
questions.explanation: Jehu the son of Hanani the seer went out to meet king Jehoshaphat.

answers.text: Micaiah the son of Imla
Elijah the prophet
Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah
Jehu the son of Hanani the seer

questions.text: What did Jehu rebuke Jehoshaphat for?
questions.explanation: Jehu asked, "Should you help the wicked, and love those who hate Yahweh?" and said that because of this wrath was on him.

answers.text: Helping the wicked and loving those who hate Yahweh
Building high places on every hill in Judah
Refusing to go to war with his own army
Taking bribes from the judges of the land

questions.text: Which good things did Jehu say were found in Jehoshaphat?
questions.explanation: Jehu said Jehoshaphat had put away the Asheroth out of the land and had set his heart to seek God.

answers.text: He had built a new temple for Yahweh in Samaria
He had defeated the Syrians without any help
He had put away the Asheroth and set his heart to seek God
He had given all his riches to the poor of the land

questions.text: Between which places did Jehoshaphat go out among the people to bring them back to Yahweh?
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat went out again among the people from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim, and brought them back to Yahweh.

answers.text: From Dan in the north to Beersheba
From Jericho to the banks of the Jordan
From Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim
From Samaria all the way to the sea

questions.text: According to Jehoshaphat, for whom did the judges judge?
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat told the judges, "you don't judge for man, but for Yahweh; and he is with you in the judgment."

answers.text: Not for man, but for Yahweh
For the king and his princes
For the elders of each city
For the people who pay them

questions.text: Whom did Jehoshaphat appoint in Jerusalem for the judgment of Yahweh and for controversies?
questions.explanation: In Jerusalem Jehoshaphat appointed Levites and priests, and some of the heads of the fathers' households of Israel, for the judgment of Yahweh and for controversies.

answers.text: Prophets, seers and the sons of the prophets
Levites, priests and heads of fathers' households
Captains of the chariots and of the army
Merchants and craftsmen from Tyre and Sidon

questions.text: What were the judges in Jerusalem to do whenever a controversy came to them from their brothers?
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat said they must warn them, that they not be guilty toward Yahweh, so that wrath would not come on them and their brothers.

answers.text: Send the matter on to the king of Israel in Samaria
Cast lots before the altar to decide the matter
Let the oldest man of the city decide the case
Warn them, so that they would not be guilty toward Yahweh

questions.text: Who was the chief priest over the judges in all matters of Yahweh?
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat said, "Amariah the chief priest is over you in all matters of Yahweh."

answers.text: Amariah
Jehoiada
Zadok
Azariah

questions.text: Who was over the judges in all the king's matters?
questions.explanation: Zebadiah the son of Ishmael, the ruler of the house of Judah, was over them in all the king's matters.

answers.text: Jehu the son of Hanani
Jahaziel the son of Zechariah
Zebadiah the son of Ishmael
Eliezer the son of Dodavahu
